speaker: tilda
text: They say a halfling put Garrick Vane in the ground. Lantern Row held a vigil.

speaker: brogan
text: Hard justice. I will not say I blame her.

speaker: tilda
text: I heard the halfling let Garrick Vane walk. Mercy, in Lantern Row!

speaker: ketter
text: It takes more nerve to spare a man than to stab him.

speaker: iolen
text: The Sisters sing free now. Harl Tollow rows out, and the water answers him.

speaker: brogan
text: Gave me goosebumps, it did.

speaker: iolen
text: The Drowned Choir sings for a master now. Harl has stopped rowing.

speaker: mosk
text: A song with a leash on it. I do not like it.

speaker: mosk
text: Ysolde's Mirror is shards on the kiln floor. The glasswright sleeps at last.

speaker: tilda
text: Silver glitter in every boot that comes up from the Glimmerdeep.

speaker: iolen
text: Someone looked into the Mirror, I am told. They came out knowing things.

speaker: ketter
text: I once saw a man go quiet after a mirror. He was never the same.

speaker: brogan
text: Odalys named the forger to their face. Pawn tickets are honest again.

speaker: tilda
text: Whoever pointed the finger had proof. Nobody is arguing.

speaker: tilda
text: The forger left town by lantern light, and Odalys looks lighter.

speaker: mosk
text: I heard coins changed hands. I heard nothing else. I heard nothing.

speaker: iolen
text: The Sunken Orchard blooms again under open sky. Silverfruit in the market!

speaker: brogan
text: One bite and my cough was gone.

speaker: iolen
text: The orchard gate stands crooked and the trees have gone quiet.

speaker: mosk
text: Somebody paid a price down there. I bar my door at night.

speaker: ketter
text: The Sergeant of the Fourth Company has his roll called at last. You gave him peace.

speaker: brogan
text: Skarn the Spider Rider is dead! The Warrens are quiet. Mostly.

speaker: tilda
text: The rats never read the news, love.

speaker: tilda
text: Old Clubtail is down! Miners say the Grotto doors open easier now.

speaker: mosk
text: Glasshide fell. The Glimmerdeep glows, and nobody has turned to glass this week.

speaker: ketter
text: Forgemaster Brakk is finished. The Ashforge anvils ring for free folk again.

speaker: tilda
text: The Dread Sovereign is dead! Somebody drinks free tonight. I hope it is you.

speaker: ketter
text: The Tyrant still sleeps under the vault, mind. Do not celebrate too long.

speaker: iolen
text: The moon looks cracked tonight. One seal is gone, they say.

speaker: brogan
text: Every third rest, another one breaks. Count your naps.

speaker: ketter
text: Three seals broken. Gorvax shifts in his sleep. Do not linger up here.

speaker: tilda
text: Odalys at the pawn shop is white as flour. Someone forged her tickets.

speaker: mosk
text: If you find the forger, she pays well. If you do not, she remembers.

speaker: ketter
text: Three leads at the pawn shop: the tickets, the grave dirt, the back alley. Check all three first.

speaker: tilda
text: Odalys wants proof, not a guess. A hasty accusation never ends well.

speaker: iolen
text: Harl Tollow rows out each dusk and listens. He swears his wife still sings under the water.

speaker: brogan
text: Down in the Drowned Grotto, second floor. You need a strong stomach.

speaker: iolen
text: The Sunken Chapel stands on the second floor. The Black Pool lies beyond it. Bring a steady heart.

speaker: ketter
text: A glasswright named Ysolde lost her trust in mirrors. The old kiln, third floor.

speaker: mosk
text: Do not look at any mirror down there longer than you must.

speaker: ketter
text: A Sergeant of the Fourth Company still walks the Ashforge, counting his dead.

speaker: brogan
text: Three tags missing from his roll. Search the old barracks.

speaker: iolen
text: A keeper named Maelis tends the Sunken Orchard on the third floor. The trees listen.

speaker: iolen
text: They answer to the hour and the weather. Read the sky and the trees before you choose.

speaker: tilda
text: Chalk marks on the cellar doors in Lantern Row. Three dots and a hook. Still fresh.

speaker: brogan
text: Garrick Vane's old crew. Eleven gone, and one man walks free.

speaker: brogan
text: Four of the Watch went into the Warrens and never came back. Rowan will not say it.

speaker: ketter
text: Bound, not dead, I would bet my knee. Cut them loose.

speaker: tilda
text: Marga hears digging under the cellar. Not rats. Someone tunnels toward the barrels.

speaker: mosk
text: First floor, I heard. Collapse it and she will never stop thanking you.

speaker: iolen
text: Brother Osric lost temple relics in a satchel stitched with the royal sun.

speaker: mosk
text: The Grotto swallowed it. Sunk in the water, but dry inside, by some blessing.

speaker: ketter
text: Dwarven smiths sit in chains at the Ashforge. Dobbin swears they will fight for you.

speaker: brogan
text: Smash the chains. Do not pick the locks.

speaker: ketter
text: First floor, the Warrens. Skarn rides a spider, and spiders burn. Bring fire.

speaker: brogan
text: Rats come in packs. Fight in the corridor, not the open room.

speaker: ketter
text: Old Clubtail hits like a falling roof. Keep your healer behind the line and topped up.

speaker: mosk
text: No healer in your party? Down in the Grotto? Old Clubtail breaks bones.

speaker: brogan
text: Hire a priest at the bar before you go. It is cheaper than a funeral.

speaker: ketter
text: Glasshide the Basilisk turns folk to glass. Thunder shatters it. Poison does nothing.

speaker: brogan
text: Gargoyles in the Glimmerdeep shrug off lightning and poison. Hit them with steel.

speaker: ketter
text: Forgemaster Brakk shrugs off fire. Odd, for a man who lives in a forge.

speaker: mosk
text: The chimera Cindermaw burns, flies and bites three ways. Cold drops it like a stone.

speaker: ketter
text: Malthrax fears radiant light and shrugs off the dark. Bring something that shines.

speaker: iolen
text: The Sovereign's staff has a crack under the third ring. Find the tall tale and strike there.

speaker: brogan
text: Another round! And a dwarf's blessing on whoever pays!

speaker: tilda
text: Pay first, bless after, Brogan.

speaker: mosk
text: Ninety gold, three pelts and a lamp. That is all I have left, and I was robbed twice.

speaker: ketter
text: Thirty years in the dungeons. My knees remember every one of them.

speaker: iolen
text: The road is long, but this tavern is warm. I rest here between pilgrimages.

speaker: tilda
text: Marga waters the ale. Do not tell her I said so.

speaker: brogan
text: I could not tell. Is that bad?

speaker: brogan
text: I heard the stew has rat in it.

speaker: tilda
text: Only on weekdays, love.

speaker: brambur
text: My mum was a smith before she was anything else. She forged a hammer for every child she blessed.

speaker: brambur
text: Someone took hers from the forge. It is somewhere below us, and I keep apologizing to the rats in case they have it.

speaker: brambur
text: If you see dwarven boot prints, will you tell me? Please? Sorry. Please.

speaker: brambur
text: I did not tell you about my father. He went down a mine and counted the dark instead of the days.

speaker: brambur
text: Mother Pellwen says every second chance is a door. I only have to knock, instead of apologizing to it.

speaker: brambur
text: I used to pray for the courage to be brave. Lately I pray for the courage to be useful.

speaker: brambur
text: You make me useful. I wanted you to know that. It is the nicest thing anyone has done for me.

speaker: brambur
text: Sorry. I mean thank you.

speaker: brambur
text: The hammer has a name. Hearthsong. My mum sang to the iron while she worked.

speaker: brambur
text: When we find it, I would like you to hear it ring. That is all. That is everything.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick's spellbook was scattered by cultists. Pages, you understand, written in his own tiny hand.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Without them Fizzwick is merely brilliant. With them, Fizzwick is inevitable.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Keep an eye out for torn pages. Fizzwick will pretend he does not care.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick was expelled from the Academy of Brightspire. Officially, for a fireball in the library.

speaker: fizzwick
text: The fireball was peer review, a rather harsh one. The library has since been rebuilt, and it is bigger.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick will tell you something he has told no one. He fears nobody remembers a gnome who is not loud.

speaker: fizzwick
text: So Fizzwick is very loud. Even in the dark. Especially in the dark.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick has never had a friend who stayed after the explosion. You stayed.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick has noted this in a footnote. It is the longest footnote he has ever written.

speaker: pip
text: The Lantern Row Crew had eleven. We lit one lantern for each of us, over the old bakery door.

speaker: pip
text: Garrick Vane was my partner, and my best friend. He sold the whole crew to the cult for a pocket of gold.

speaker: pip
text: So I follow the Lantern Row marks down the floors. Three clues, then the Seneschal's door.

speaker: pip
text: Posy was the youngest. Nine years old, pockets like a magician. Garrick swore he would keep her safe.

speaker: pip
text: I do not want to talk about Posy. Thank you for not making me.

speaker: pip
text: Some nights I plan to stab him. Some nights I plan to hear him say sorry.

speaker: pip
text: I like the second plan less. Whatever you decide when we get there, I will remember it. I remember everything.

speaker: pip
text: I do not trust anybody. But I trust you a little. For me, that is a lot.

speaker: pip
text: When we reach the Seneschal's door, stand where I can see you. That is all I ask.

speaker: grumsh
text: I am writing a ballad. One verse for every floor of the Blackspire. Five verses, no chorus.

speaker: grumsh
text: My mother wanted a bard. I am a disappointment with a very good rhyme for slaughter.

speaker: grumsh
text: If you find a verse on a wall, in a carving or a drunk's scrawl, tell me. It may be the one.

speaker: grumsh
text: My father was a warlord. He taught me to count enemies. My mother taught me to count syllables.

speaker: grumsh
text: I am better at the second. No one has ever cheered a syllable.

speaker: grumsh
text: When I was small, I sang to the wounded in the camp. They said I sounded like a kind storm.

speaker: grumsh
text: Then my father heard. He called it weakness, and I put the songs away for twenty years.

speaker: grumsh
text: Last night I hummed in my sleep. Brambur says it was lovely.

speaker: grumsh
text: I will sing the ballad aloud when we win. You may stand at the back. I will still see you.

speaker: zizzy
text: Zizzy needs blasting powder! Dwarven blasting powder, the good stuff, in the Ashforge somewhere!

speaker: zizzy
text: The Ashforge gate is locked. Locks are just very small walls, and walls are very slow explosions.

speaker: zizzy
text: Find the powder and Zizzy will make you a firework. A tiny one. Medium.

speaker: zizzy
text: My family did not like the fire. The tiefling parts of me that go boom. They told me to hide it.

speaker: zizzy
text: Zizzy did not hide it. Zizzy made it a hobby, then a career. Look how well it is going!

speaker: zizzy
text: Zizzy has a secret. When it is quiet, I get scared the fire will not stop.

speaker: zizzy
text: When you are near, it stays small. I do not know why. I am not complaining. Do not tell Vexrath, he will file it.

speaker: zizzy
text: Zizzy made you a gift. A very small firework, shaped like a heart. It exploded. Sorry!

speaker: zizzy
text: I will make another. You are my favorite explosion and my favorite person, in that order.

speaker: vexrath
text: My clan was exiled by royal decree, forty years ago. I have read the decree. I believe it is forged.

speaker: vexrath
text: The original is sealed in crystal somewhere on the third floor. I will find it, or I will file a complaint.

speaker: vexrath
text: If you see a royal seal, bring it to me. Bring it gently. It is evidence.

speaker: vexrath
text: Ledgerus teaches that every promise is a debt, and every debt will be called. I take that seriously.

speaker: vexrath
text: I fear I have not always kept my promises to my own family.

speaker: vexrath
text: My sister begged me not to sign the exile. I signed. I thought it was the law. It was a lie.

speaker: vexrath
text: I have been filing that mistake in my heart for forty years. It has no folder.

speaker: vexrath
text: I have drafted a document. It is a character reference. It is for you.

speaker: vexrath
text: It reads, in full: honest, brave, irregular. Please note that I have stamped it twice.

speaker: nettle
text: I am collecting the true legend of the Sovereign's staff. One fragment per floor, from the second floor down.

speaker: nettle
text: Everyone agrees on the staff. Nobody agrees on the details. That is how you know it is true.

speaker: nettle
text: If a smith or a ghost starts talking, listen. I pay in stories.

speaker: nettle
text: Truth time. I did not invent the door. I only wanted to be the sort of person who might have.

speaker: nettle
text: Everything else I told you is true. Possibly. That is the truth.

speaker: nettle
text: I grew up in a ship's galley. My mother sold stories to sailors for an extra ladle of soup.

speaker: nettle
text: She said a lie is a gift when you give it away. I have given away a great many gifts.

speaker: nettle
text: I tried writing the true story of this party. It came out better than any lie I own.

speaker: nettle
text: I am keeping it. Somebody should remember us properly, and it might as well be a liar.

speaker: brambur
text: Any word of dwarven boot prints? Mum's hammer is out there, on the first floor, and the fourth.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick's missing pages are on the second floor and the third. Torn, in tiny handwriting. You cannot miss them.

speaker: pip
text: The Lantern Row marks are on every floor. Three clues, then the Seneschal's door.

speaker: grumsh
text: There is a verse waiting on every floor. Wall carvings, drunken scrawls. I will know it when I hear it.

speaker: zizzy
text: Blasting powder, in the Ashforge! A keg, a barrel! Zizzy would settle for a thimble.

speaker: vexrath
text: The original decree is sealed in crystal on the third floor. I would know the seal anywhere.

speaker: nettle
text: One tale fragment per floor, from the second down. Ask the smiths and the ghosts. They love a story.

speaker: pip
text: Traps on this floor like dull corridors. Walk slowly, listen for clicks, and check the plate stones.

speaker: zizzy
text: The spiders on this floor burn! Zizzy will bring the fire. The rats burn too, but they do not enjoy it.

speaker: brambur
text: Old Clubtail hits very hard. Keep us healed, and keep the healer standing. That is me. Sorry.

speaker: liora
text: The Grotto floods in places. Look for the chapel and the black pool, and listen for singing.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Wasps and water. Fizzwick advises thunder, or at least dry socks.

speaker: vexrath
text: Glasshide turns the careless to glass. Thunder shatters it. Poison does nothing. I have filed this.

speaker: nettle
text: The orchard in the Glimmerdeep is real, and so is the kiln. Look for open sky and a glint of silver.

speaker: pip
text: The mirrors on this floor lie. Do not stare at one longer than a breath.

speaker: zizzy
text: Cindermaw hates cold! Zizzy has no cold. Zizzy has other fun things.

speaker: grumsh
text: Brakk wears fire like a coat. Steel or cold, not flame. I will write him a short verse.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Smiths in chains. Fizzwick does not enjoy chains. Free them, and they will help us.

speaker: liora
text: Malthrax hates radiant light, and the dark does nothing. If you have anything holy, save it for him.

speaker: nettle
text: The staff has a crack under the third ring. Strike there and it ends. I have it on good authority.

speaker: pip
text: The Seneschal's door is somewhere on this floor. Check every wall before you check every door.

speaker: brambur
text: Rest before you push on, please. A tired party is a sorry party. I am saying sorry in advance.

speaker: fizzwick
text: Fizzwick advises you to read the walls. Walls are the oldest books, and the rudest.

speaker: pip
text: Check every chest twice and every door once. Then check your own pockets.

speaker: grumsh
text: Fight with your back to a wall. Make the enemy walk around your rhyme.

speaker: zizzy
text: If it is stuck, burn it. If it is not stuck, ask first. Mostly burn.

speaker: vexrath
text: Prepare, then proceed. A properly prepared slate of spells wins more fights than courage.

speaker: nettle
text: When in doubt, ask the ghosts. They love to talk, and they never charge.

speaker: liora
text: Watch for loose stones, cold drafts and fresh footprints. The floor always tells the truth.
